title: Formal unramifiedness on etale scheme charts
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:Z\to X$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A first-order thickening is a representable closed immersion with square-zero ideal, tested after scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Say that $f$ is formally unramified if restriction $\operatorname{Hom}_X(T',Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}_X(T,Z)$ is injective for every such thickening $T\hookrightarrow T'$ of affine schemes over $X$. For a scheme morphism this agrees with [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism]. The following are equivalent: (1) $f$ is formally unramified; (2) for every commutative square $V\xrightarrow{g}U$ over $Z\xrightarrow{f}X$, where $V,U$ are schemes and $V\to Z$, $U\to X$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], the scheme map $g$ is formally unramified; (3) there is such a square with both vertical maps surjective and $g$ formally unramified. Fibre products used to form charts are [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. No local finite type, quasi-compactness or separation hypothesis is required.

proof.text: First record the direct scheme specialization needed below. If $p:E\to Y$ is representable etale, $i:T\hookrightarrow T'$ is a first-order thickening of affine schemes, and $e_0:T\to E$, $b:T'\to Y$ satisfy $pe_0=bi$, then $P=T'\times_YE$ is a scheme etale over $T'$ by the meaning of representable etale in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its projection is flat and unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The pair $(i,e_0)$ gives a map $T\to P$ over $T'$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-unramified-formally-etale] to $P\to T'$ with base scheme $T'$ and test thickening $i$: it gives exactly one section $T'\to P$ extending this map. By the fibre-product universal property, sections are exactly maps $e:T'\to E$ with $pe=b$, and the extension condition is $ei=e_0$. Thus representable etale maps have the required unique lifts. This is an application to one scheme base change, with no descent or chartwise lifting theorem.

source.place: Tag 04AL, lemma-representable-property-formally-property, etale clause and its proof by the scheme base change; more-morphisms.tex Tags 02HM and 04FF.

proof.text: Assume (1), and write a square of (2) as $qg=fp$, with $p:V\to Z$ and $q:U\to X$ representable etale. For a test thickening $i:T\hookrightarrow T'$ and two maps $v_1,v_2:T'\to V$ having the same restriction to $T$ and satisfying $gv_1=gv_2$, the equality $fpv_1=qgv_1=qgv_2=fpv_2$ and (1) give $pv_1=pv_2$. Apply the uniqueness in step 1 to $p$, with this common base map $T'\to Z$ and common restriction $T\to V$. It gives $v_1=v_2$. This is precisely formal unramifiedness of $g$ in [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism], so (2) holds. When the original map is a scheme map, its square-zero injectivity condition likewise is exactly this definition.

source.place: Tag 04G8, lemma-formally-unramified, (1) implies (2); the composition and cancellation arguments of Tags 049T and 04G5 are written out as equalities of lifts.

proof.text: Assume (2). Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $q:U\to X$ from [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The final assertion of [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts], applied to $f:Z\to X$ and this prescribed atlas, supplies a scheme $V$, a surjective etale atlas $p:V\to Z$, and $g:V\to U$ with $qg=fp$. Condition (2) applies to this square and makes $g$ formally unramified, proving (3). Only the existence clause of the cited node is used; no unramifiedness hypothesis on $f$ is required.

source.place: Tag 04G8, lemma-formally-unramified, (2) implies (3); spaces.tex Tag 02X1, lemma-lift-morphism-presentations.

proof.text: Assume (3), fixing $p,q,g$ as above. Let $i:T\hookrightarrow T'$ be an affine first-order thickening and $a,b:T'\to Z$ satisfy $ai=bi$ and $fa=fb$. Base change the cover $p$ along $a$: by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $W'=T'\times_{a,Z}V\to T'$ is a surjective etale map from a scheme. Choose affine open subsets $A_\lambda\subset W'$ covering $W'$; their maps $r_\lambda:A_\lambda\to T'$ are jointly surjective etale, by the open-immersion and composition clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Put $A_{0,\lambda}=A_\lambda\times_{T'}T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-first-order-thickening-base-change] this is a first-order thickening of $A_\lambda$; it is affine since a closed subscheme of an affine is affine [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. The canonical map $v_\lambda:A_\lambda\to V$ lies over $ar_\lambda$. Its restriction to $A_{0,\lambda}$ also lies over $br_\lambda$ because $ai=bi$. Step 1 for $p$ therefore gives $w_\lambda:A_\lambda\to V$ over $br_\lambda$ with the same restriction. Since $qgv_\lambda=far_\lambda=fbr_\lambda=qgw_\lambda$, uniqueness in step 1 for $q$ gives $gv_\lambda=gw_\lambda$. Formal unramifiedness of the scheme map $g$ [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism] now gives $v_\lambda=w_\lambda$, whence $ar_\lambda=pv_\lambda=pw_\lambda=br_\lambda$.

proof.text: Each $r_\lambda$ in step 4 is flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], so their joint surjectivity makes them an fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site]. The algebraic space $Z$ is an fppf sheaf of sets [def-trf-algebraic-space]; its sheaf axiom says that restriction to this cover is injective. The equalities $ar_\lambda=br_\lambda$ therefore imply $a=b$. This proves (1). Empty schemes cause no exception: injectivity for the empty covering says a sheaf has a singleton value on the empty scheme. All lifting tests above used affine square-zero thickenings and no finiteness or separation assumption on $f$.
